title: Database connection pool exhausted — order-processing-api
symptoms: p99 API latency exceeds 12 s (baseline: 180 ms)
Requests queuing behind connection pool; 503 errors rising
Order checkout success rate dropped from 99.2 % to 61 %
logs: [08:14:02] WARN  order-api: connection pool exhausted, waiting for available slot (timeout=5s)
[08:14:07] ERROR order-api: PoolTimeout acquiring connection after 5000 ms
[08:14:09] WARN  postgres: remaining connection slots reserved for replication
[08:15:22] WARN  order-api: slow query detected (4312 ms): SELECT * FROM products WHERE id=?
[08:15:22] WARN  order-api: slow query detected (4289 ms): SELECT * FROM products WHERE id=?
[08:15:22] WARN  order-api: slow query detected (4301 ms): SELECT * FROM products WHERE id=?

recent_deploys.description: Checkout flow refactor: new get_order_items() method in checkout_flow.py

_ground_truth.root_cause: N+1 query regression introduced in v2.4.1. checkout_flow.get_order_items() iterates over order items and issues a separate SELECT query per item against the products table rather than a single batched query. Under typical load (15–20 items per order) this generates 15–20 concurrent queries per checkout request, saturating the 20-connection pool.
resolution_steps: Option A (immediate): roll back to v2.4.0 via the CI pipeline rollback command.
Option B (fix forward): in checkout_flow.py line 142, replace per-item SELECT with a single IN-clause query: `Product.objects.filter(id__in=item_ids).all()` (Django ORM) or equivalent join.
Verify fix by re-running the checkout load test; pool idle connections should return above 10.
